messages:
Elliot Price: Need to sync on docs surfaces for the VPC Terraform modules. We’ve got Confluence deployment guide + the docs-site quickstart PR (redwood-docs/#20612). Right now they read a bit different + not super clear what’s alpha vs “supported”. Can we align today?

Kira Thompson: yup. I’m in the Confluence guide (`eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/terraform-vpc-deployment-guide-alpha`). It assumes EKS + private subnets + endpoints, and has some internal-only notes (installer handoff, Slack escalation). Docs-site quickstart reads more like customer-facing.

Markus Klein: +1 from field: we need something we can share with design partners without them thinking it’s GA. The quickest way is a single “alpha banner” and consistent language across both.

Vivek Kulkarni: Agree. For alpha: docs are primarily for design partners + internal SE/PS. We should explicitly say: “alpha, best-effort support, expect changes, pin versions.” Also we should not promise VPN/DX “works” beyond placeholders.

Irene Choi: Also accuracy: Confluence guide currently says “one NAT per AZ recommended” but modules default is “one NAT per AZ if `nat_strategy = per_az` else single NAT”. Some customers will choose single NAT for cost. We need the same wording.

Bruno Silva: On docs-site quickstart I mentioned “NAT per AZ (default)” because that was earlier draft. I can change to: “default per_az” if that’s still true in main. (Need to verify after pr-18605 fix.)

Sahana Iyer: FYI CI pinned provider versions + we’re calling this “alpha” everywhere in `redwood-terraform` now, but docs-site page should also state min Terraform + AWS provider versions. Otherwise we get support pings when validate fails.

Simran Kaur: Another mismatch: Confluence guide has a longer “Networking prereqs” section (endpoints list, DNS resolver behaviors). Docs-site page currently just says “enable endpoints” but doesn’t list the required ones. We should list the required endpoints and mark others as optional.

Elliot Price: Ok proposal:
- Confluence = canonical internal runbook style, but still should be shareable in parts.
- Docs-site quickstart = short “getting started” with strong alpha banner.
- Both link to same “Supported topologies + extension points” section in the repo README.
- Both use identical “Required endpoints” list + DNS note.

Kira Thompson: Works. For Confluence I can split “internal ops + escalation” into a clearly marked section at bottom (“Redwood internal only”), so the top is safe to share.

Markus Klein: pls also add “What we do NOT support in alpha” in both places, super explicit:
- no multi-region
- no custom shared VPC / transit gateway permutations (we can advise but not in module defaults)
- no hard guarantee on customer proxy/egress appliances

Vivek Kulkarni: + add “Design partner only / contact Redwood to proceed” line. We’ve had people forwarding quickstarts around.

Irene Choi: On endpoint list: I’d like the docs to call out ECR (api + dkr) + STS + CloudWatch Logs as the common failure mode. We just had the installer change to detect missing ECR endpoints and warn, but docs should still prevent it.

Bruno Silva: I can paste the current endpoint defaults from the module readme here. One sec.

Bruno Silva: Current endpoints we enable in examples:
- `com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` (Gateway)
- `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api` (Interface)
- `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr` (Interface)
- `com.amazonaws.<region>.sts` (Interface)
- `com.amazonaws.<region>.logs` (Interface)
Optional/depends:
- `ec2`, `autoscaling`, `elasticloadbalancing` (if customer blocks public egress heavily)
- `kms` (if using CMKs for EBS / secrets)

Simran Kaur: Please add the DNS caveat: if using interface endpoints, private DNS must be enabled OR customer must provide conditional forwarders / Route53 Resolver rules. Otherwise pulls fail intermittently and it looks like “random DNS flake”.

Sahana Iyer: + we should keep the exact phrasing aligned with installer preflight docs. The installer doc PR (redwood-private-installer/#19144) uses “Required: ecr.api, ecr.dkr, s3 gateway”. If docs-site says more, people think installer is incomplete.

Elliot Price: Great point. We can phrase like:
“Minimum required for installer: S3 gateway + ECR endpoints (api+dkr) with private DNS. Recommended for fully-private: STS + CloudWatch Logs; plus others depending on your controls.”

Kira Thompson: Confluence guide currently implies “CloudWatch Logs required”. I’ll change to “recommended” with rationale (Flow logs to CW, etc.). For audit posture we can say “choose CW or S3; default retention X; confirm with sec team.”

Markus Klein: Field note: customers *will* ask “where do logs go by default”. Put it up front:
- Flow logs default destination
- Retention default
- Who owns the bucket/log group

Irene Choi: Careful there: we intentionally default to customer-owned destinations for S3. For CW we create a log group but still in customer account. Docs should say “all logs stay in your AWS account; Redwood does not receive VPC flow logs.”

Vivek Kulkarni: Yes, and label “alpha defaults may change” (esp retention). Naomi will want that statement.

Elliot Price: On “alpha labeling” specifically:
- Docs-site: add an “Alpha” badge + callout at top: “This guide covers Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha). Expect breaking changes; pin module versions; contact your Redwood team.”
- Confluence: add same callout at top.
- Both: link to release notes page for “alpha release notes”.

Simran Kaur: + add: “If you are NOT a design partner, use existing Private deployment networking checklist” (otherwise we’ll confuse GA path).

Bruno Silva: Quickstart currently has a “Minimal tfvars” snippet. It includes `enable_vpn_placeholders = true` which might be misleading. Should we remove for alpha docs-site?

Markus Klein: remove. That knob reads as “VPN supported”. We can leave a sentence: “There are placeholders/outputs for integrating with VPN/DX; consult your network team.”

Irene Choi: +1 remove from minimal. Keep it in “Extension points” section.

Sahana Iyer: Agree. Also include provider/version block in quickstart. Something like:
```
terraform { required_version = ">= 1.6.0" }
provider "aws" { version = "~> 5.4" }
```
(or whatever is in repo). People copy/paste.

Kira Thompson: Action items?
- I’ll update Confluence guide: add alpha banner, fix NAT wording, split internal-only section, align endpoints list + DNS note.

Elliot Price: I’ll update docs-site PR #20612: add alpha badge/banner, add versions/prereqs, rewrite endpoints section to match installer docs, remove vpn knob from minimal, add “not GA” language.

Bruno Silva: I’ll sanity check module defaults (NAT strategy + endpoints) against main + ping you exact text to use. Also can add a snippet to `redwood-terraform` README so we can link to canonical “Required endpoints” list.

Markus Klein: I’ll send a short “shareable blurb” SE can paste into emails: “alpha, pin versions, design partner only, support path”.

Simran Kaur: I can do a quick review of both for architecture correctness once edits are up.

Elliot Price: Cool. Can we timebox: edits by EOD tomorrow, review Thurs, merge Fri?

Kira Thompson: works

Irene Choi: works

Sahana Iyer: works. pls tag me on docs PR if you change version numbers.

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: (and ty)

Elliot Price: (small thing) For docs-site, do we explicitly say “AWS only (alpha)”?

Vivek Kulkarni: Yes. One line: “Alpha scope: AWS VPC only. GCP/Azure stubs/roadmap.”

Kira Thompson: Adding.

Bruno Silva: Adding.

Elliot Price: ok closing loop. I’ll post updates in thread when PR is ready for review.

Elliot Price: Update: pushed commits to redwood-docs/#20612 with alpha banner + new endpoints wording. Still need to add provider version block.

Sahana Iyer: saw it. Provider versions in repo are `terraform >= 1.6.2` and aws `~> 5.31` (from CI). Use those, please.

Elliot Price: ty, will update.

Kira Thompson: Confluence guide updated as well. NAT wording fixed + “internal only” section moved to bottom. Added “Minimum endpoints for installer” list + DNS note.

Simran Kaur: skimmed Confluence updates, looks good. One tweak: in DNS note, call out Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints as an *option* for corp DNS, not required.

Kira Thompson: yep will adjust.

Markus Klein: Blurb for SE/PS (shareable):
“Redwood Private VPC Terraform Modules are in **Alpha** for design partners. Please **pin module versions** and expect iterative changes. This guide covers the AWS-only alpha footprint (VPC/subnets/NAT, endpoints, logging, IAM scaffold). VPN/Direct Connect integrations are supported via documented extension points; topologies outside the reference architecture are best-effort.”

Elliot Price: Perfect. I’ll add a shortened version in the docs-site banner.

Elliot Price: Final update: docs-site PR now includes provider versions + AWS-only alpha scope line. Ready for review from @Simran @Irene @Vivek.

Irene Choi: reviewed, LGTM. The “Recommended endpoints” list is clear now.

Vivek Kulkarni: LGTM. Please ensure the banner says “contact your Redwood team” vs generic support.

Elliot Price: updated banner text. Merging once CI passes.

Bruno Silva: Also merged a small README tweak in `redwood-terraform` so both pages can deep-link to the canonical endpoints section.

Elliot Price: nice. thanks all.
